subject: Sprint capacity allowance + invoice offset for Feb campaign
messages:
From: Emma Park <emma@brightlens.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightlens.com
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Quick request — temporary capacity for Feb campaign

Hi Soojin,

We have a product marketing sprint starting next Monday (Feb 15) that will send several high-traffic campaigns over a 72-hour window. Based on our forecast the peak will be roughly 6x our current sustained throughput, mostly short-lived spikes.

Can Redwood provide a temporary allowance for that three-day window and either prorate the uplift or apply a one-off credit? Procurement asked me to get a written confirmation we can rely on extra quota (and the approximate surcharge) before they approve the special billable card for this spend.

Attached is last week's usage for reference (CSV). We can be flexible on model variant if it helps price-wise, but low latency is important for this campaign.

Thanks — Emma
Product Lead, BrightLens

Attachment: BrightLens_usage-feb-week1.csv (CSV, 42 KB)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Emma Park <emma@brightlens.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 10:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick request — temporary capacity for Feb campaign

Hi Emma — thanks for the heads-up and the CSV. We can absolutely support a short-window uplift. Two quick notes up front:

- We have a "sprint allowance" play for exactly this scenario — short-lived quota increases up to a defined headroom with a simple invoice offset/credit model.
- To preserve latency SLOs during the window we may route to a slightly larger instance type; that affects unit rates.

Proposal (tentative):
1) Temporary quota uplift to 6x baseline for 72 hours (Feb 15 00:00 UTC — Feb 18 00:00 UTC).
2) Bill at the elevated rate for tokens used during the window but apply a sprint credit equal to 30% of the uplifted spend (applied as an invoice offset on next invoice).
3) No change to monthly commit — this is an add-on one-off.

I've attached a short amendment draft (proposed-amendment-sprint-credit.pdf) and flagged finance for guidance. If you can confirm the exact campaign UTC window and expected peak token/sec, I'll lock the uplift and send a DocuSign link.

Quick question for procurement: do you need the DocuSign before the window to pre-authorize charges, or is a signed amendment + post-window invoice offset acceptable?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-amendment-sprint-credit.pdf

From: Emma Park <emma@brightlens.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightlens.com
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick request — temporary capacity for Feb campaign

Hi Soojin — thanks, that looks sensible. Procurement said they'll need DocuSign signatures before the window to allow the card to be used, otherwise finance won't clear the charge.

We can accept the 30% sprint credit if legal signs off on the amendment. I'll confirm the exact UTC window by EOD tomorrow and send an estimate of peak token/sec.

— Emma

On a related note: would Redwood consider a smaller discount (e.g., 10% additional) if we commit to a 3-month steady-state increase post-sprint? That could move us toward a short-term committed uplift.

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: BrightLens sprint — approval + discount ask

Ben / Lauren — forwarding BrightLens thread. Key asks: temporary 6x quota for 72 hours, signed DocuSign pre-authorize, and a commercial ask for an extra 10% discount if they convert to a 3-month commit after the sprint.

Can finance confirm if applying a 30% invoice offset is ok for that uplift (we'd fund the remainder into the invoice schedule), and can sales/legal greenlight a conditional 10% short-term conversion discount (we'd need to define minima and rollback clauses)?

Notes: latency SLO is important — recommend we route to a larger instance family for the window (Ben pls confirm ops impact). I flagged the amendment PDF; legal will need to confirm the language for a conversion-triggered discount.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — doc needs signatures by Feb 12 to make procurement's cutoff.

Thanks,
Soojin

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightLens sprint — approval + discount ask

Quick update — finance ok with the 30% sprint credit as an invoice offset for one-off uplift; we just need the amendment to include a reconciliation clause (we reconcile actual uplift tokens vs estimated after window and adjust credit if variance >15%). Ops confirms we can provision the larger instance family for the window; expect a ~12% unit cost increase on elevated routes.

Commercial: we can offer a conditional 10% conversion discount if they sign a minimum 3-month committed uplift at a specified baseline within 14 days after the sprint. Legal will add the conversion trigger and a 30-day rollback provision.

Soojin — send the DocuSign link with the attached amendment (I've updated the reconcile language) and ask procurement to sign before Feb 12. I'll loop Legal on the DocuSign envelope.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
